goal.text: Make room for the readers and the frost wyrm without waking the old ice.

voiceGuide.tone: Warm, curious and practical. Short sentences. Show the consequence of each plan. Nobody dies.

arrival.narration: Beyond the memory reading room, yeti builders have stopped carving a new chamber for the memory readers. A frost wyrm has curled across their doorway, using a bench as a pillow. Its breath covers the wall in tiny ice ferns. "Make room for us and the wyrm without waking the old ice," says a builder. "We can move the room. We cannot ask the mountain for a second mountain." The wyrm opens one eye. Pip stays in the old reading room to help the elder sort the notes while you work below.

listen.narration: The builder raises a quiet hand. Every scrape makes the wyrm tighten around the doorway. How will you approach without making the trouble louder?

choices.label: Wrap the loose tools before moving closer
Follow the soft snow beside the wall

listen_1.narration: You wrap the chisels in a spare blanket. The builder looks relieved. The largest chisel has its own knitted hat.

listen_2.narration: You leave the tools where they are and take the snow strip. Your steps make shallow dimples instead of sharp echoes.

watch.narration: The nest blocks the doorway, not the whole tunnel. The wyrm watches anyone near the bench. You can observe its tail from the far wall or check the scrape marks beside the doorway.

choices.label: Watch where the tail moves when someone steps back
Compare the marks without touching the nest

watch_1.narration: You retreat one pace. The tail loosens. The wyrm is keeping a space, not chasing travelers down the tunnel.

watch_2.narration: You study the scraped snow from the safe strip. Most marks curve around the bench. A small builder's stool sits outside them, politely ignored.

watch_check.prompt: Mark the reach of the nest from ground the wyrm leaves clear.

onSuccess.narration: Your marks stay outside the turning tail.

onFailure.narration: The tail shifts farther than your first mark.

watch_clear.narration: The builders can see where the wyrm needs space. Nobody needs to test the mark with a foot.

watch_changed.narration: You erase the guessed mark and leave a wider margin. The builder moves the stool back with a hooked stick.

supplies.narration: Two things lie outside the nest: a bundle of carving tools and a folded wall plan. The builders can reach either, but the wyrm keeps turning toward the noise. Which will you move first?

choices.label: Carry the wrapped tools out along the snow strip
Roll the wall plan away from the nest

supplies_1.narration: You pass the quiet bundle along the wall. One chisel hat has slipped over its point. The builder fixes it before anyone picks the bundle up.

supplies_2.narration: You roll the plan from its far end. The builders will know where to start again, even if this doorway stays occupied.

cold_opening.narration: In the far wall, an opening shows an empty snow hollow sheltered from wind. The Listening Chime, the chime from the glacier travelers, returns a clear echo. A builder can see both sides from the tunnel. How will you check that the hollow is unoccupied? On your side of the opening, loose bones rattle in a heap. The builders have stopped work around them; nobody knows where they came from.

choices.label: Watch the whole floor through the opening
Ask a builder to signal from the far side
Have a starweaver study the opening

cold_opening_1.narration: You wait for blowing snow to clear. There are no tracks, nests or stored tools in the hollow. A lump shaped like a boot is only snow.

cold_opening_2.narration: A builder steps through, leaves a marker and comes back while you watch. The way remains open. Nobody promises it will obey a new command.

cold_opening_3.narration: A starweaver studies the light privately. The builders check the ground and the echo with the rest of the party. Everyone agrees on what the hollow can safely hold.

cold_opening_check.prompt: Compare the hollow's floor and shelter with the wyrm's present nesting space.

onSuccess.narration: The hollow has room for the whole curling tail.

onFailure.narration: Drifting snow hides the far edge.

cold_opening_clear.narration: You mark a clear sheltered space beyond the opening. Moving the wyrm there is possible; forcing it to like the place is not.

cold_opening_changed.narration: The builder clears the drift with a long pole, then marks a wider clear space. You wait for the check rather than guessing.

bed.narration: The hollow has hard snow and no bench pillow. If you try moving the wyrm, it needs a place to settle. If you drive it off instead, the hollow will still leave it shelter away from the readers.

choices.label: Spread clean snow into a shallow bowl
Set a broad ice slab below the wind lip

bed_1.narration: You shape the hollow from the open side without taking anything from the nest. The builder smooths one edge with a shovel the size of a soup spoon.

bed_2.narration: You slide a loose slab into the hollow while the builder steadies it. It offers a flat resting place without blocking the return opening.

lanes.narration: The builders need one lane to withdraw and another that leads the wyrm toward the hollow. The paths must not cross. How will you mark them?

choices.label: Lay cloth along the people's lane
Cut shallow grooves along the empty lane

lanes_1.narration: You lay cloth from the doorway to the snow strip. The wyrm's lane stays broad and empty. The builder straightens a corner that looks too much like a snack.

lanes_2.narration: You scrape only the soft new snow. The lane curves toward the opening without pointing at the old ice.

lanes_check.prompt: Slide the loose benches away so the two lanes stay separate.

onSuccess.narration: The benches move without a sharp scrape.

onFailure.narration: One bench catches and the wyrm raises its head.

lanes_clear.narration: Both lanes are clear, with no builder standing between the wyrm and shelter.

lanes_changed.narration: You stop instead of hauling. The builders pad the caught foot and ease the bench away while the wyrm settles.

rest.narration: The builders lead you into a side alcove, away from the nest. They share oat cakes from a tool tin scrubbed clean for lunches. You rest on folded work blankets. One cake has the shape of a very blunt chisel.

rest_watch.narration: You sit beside the alcove lamp while a builder takes the next watch. A drip taps the lunch tin like a tiny clock. You eat before the tin can count your cake away.

signal.narration: The builders stand behind the cleared benches. They can help by holding the quiet lane or signaling when the hollow is clear. Which job will they take?

choices.label: Ask them to keep the people's lane open
Ask them to watch the empty hollow

signal_1.narration: The builders take turns watching the marked lane. One solemnly removes a lunch bag from the route. It was never a good barrier.

signal_2.narration: A builder stands where both hollow and tunnel are visible. A raised mitten will mean wait; an open palm will mean clear.

offer.narration: You are ready to make space. Drive the wyrm away from the doorway, or hold the hollow's approach long enough for it to follow into shelter. Both happen on the board; the wyrm may resist. Which plan will you start with?

choices.label: Make a firm line and drive it from the doorway
Hold the quiet approach to invite it into the hollow

offer_1.narration: You leave the hollow's approach open while standing between the nest and the readers. Nobody corners the wyrm against the old ice.

offer_2.narration: You keep the hollow visible and leave the wyrm an open route. The builders stay behind the benches. A mitten waits for the first signal.

fight.narration: The frost wyrm rises from the bench. The restless bones you heard beside the opening rise and rattle. Drive them off, or hold the hollow approach for two clear rounds to guide it into a new home. The slick strip near its nest slows anyone who stops there.

room_clear.narration: The doorway is clear and the builders lower their mittens. The new room can be used without squeezing past a turning tail. The bench has a frost-wyrm-shaped dent; the builders decide it is now a special chair.

variants.text: The wyrm settles in the sheltered hollow through the opening. When a builder hums from the tunnel, it answers softly. You have a neighbor who will remember being given room.
The wyrm backs into the broad outer tunnel, leaving the readers' doorway. The builders leave the sheltered hollow available. It has not chosen the hollow.

room_moved.narration: The wyrm holds its doorway and your party withdraws behind the benches. The builders help you rest, then unroll the wall plan. "The room can go here," one says, pointing down the clear tunnel. The new reading room will open later, away from the nest. Nobody is sent back into the fight.

tools.narration: The carving tools wait beside the quiet lane. Before carrying them farther, the builders want to know whether the nearest wall is safe to work. How will you check it?

choices.label: Test only the new surface with a padded tapping block
Check the fresh cracks by lamplight

tools_1.narration: You tap the recently carved edge. The deep old ice stays untouched. A builder listens with one mitten pressed flat against the wall.

tools_2.narration: You move the lamp across the new surface. Fresh snow in a crack shows where the bench pressed, without asking the old ice for an answer.

tools_check.prompt: Mark the fresh cracks that builders must leave alone.

onSuccess.narration: You mark each fresh crack without covering it.

onFailure.narration: A shadow looks like a crack until the lamp shifts.

tools_clear.narration: The builders have a clear working area and a marked edge they will not carve past.

tools_changed.narration: You move the lamp from both sides. The builder checks your final marks before any chisel is unwrapped.

shelves.narration: The readers need somewhere to put their memory notes. A low shelf can rest on blocks, or the notes can stay on a broad table until the new wall is ready. Which will you help set up?

choices.label: Set a low shelf on wide blocks
Put the notes on the broad table for now

variants.text: The new site needs more carving, and its floor cannot hold shelf blocks yet. For now only the broad table fits in the old room. The builders must finish the new chamber after you leave.

shelves_1.narration: You stack the blocks where the floor is sound. The shortest reader can reach the shelf without sitting on anyone's shoulders.

shelves_2.narration: You clear the table and mark it for notes. A builder moves a spare bench away from the writing side.

shelves_check.prompt: Set the furniture level on the marked sound floor.

onSuccess.narration: The furniture stays level when the builder tests its edge.

onFailure.narration: One foot rocks on a patch of loose snow.

shelves_clear.narration: The notes have a steady place, clear of the working lane.

shelves_changed.narration: You sweep the loose snow away and use lower blocks. The furniture sits flatter, and everybody's toes are happier.

readers.narration: The first readers wait in the old reading room. They need a route that avoids the nest, wherever the new furniture stands. How will you guide them?

choices.label: Walk the clear lane before inviting them along
Post a builder at each blind corner

readers_1.narration: You follow the marked lane all the way. At the last turn you check back, making sure the route is visible from reader height.

readers_2.narration: You place the builders where a reader can see the next mitten. The signals are far easier to follow than the builders' first attempt at arrows.

readers_check.prompt: Lead a quiet walking rhythm so readers can follow without a loud call.

onSuccess.narration: The readers follow the rhythm through the cleared lane.

onFailure.narration: The first rhythm is too fast for the furniture carriers.

readers_clear.narration: The readers reach their safe working place with their notes.

variants.text: Their working place is a crowded corner of the old room. The new chamber is still a building job, with tools and blankets needed for another day.

readers_changed.narration: You slow the rhythm and carry the broad table in turns. The readers reach their working place without crossing the nest.

quiet.narration: The elder comes down from the old reading room and repeats the warning from the memory ice: do not shout near the old layers. This room has solved a small problem; the mountain still holds things nobody understands. What will you leave for the next visitors?

choices.label: A picture of the quiet route and the nest boundary
A simple note asking visitors to lower their voices

quiet_1.narration: You draw the benches and the safe lane. You leave the oldest ice blank, because blank is more honest than an invented answer.

quiet_2.narration: You write the quiet request beside a drawing of a mitten. The builder adds a tiny hat to the picture of the chisel.

neighbors.narration: The builders will keep watching the nest and the sheltered hollow. Your work here should tell them what to do next, not pretend the wyrm has vanished from the mountain.

choices.label: Ask them to leave the shelter approach open
Ask them to keep the readers' lane clear each morning

neighbors_1.narration: The builders mark the approach on the wall plan. They will check it quietly before carrying tools that way.

neighbors_2.narration: A builder takes the first watch. She moves her own lunch bag off the marked lane before you can point at it.

departure.narration: The builders trade rescue signals with griffins at the Cairnstep, the mountain pass. That route can carry your news toward the sky. The path behind you returns to the memory readers. How will you prepare to leave?

choices.label: Send the rescue partners a clear route report
Carry the updated wall plan back to the readers

variants.text: A new visitor follows your bench diagram to the safe lane. The builder can use your picture while keeping her voice low.
A new visitor sees your mitten sign and lowers their voice before the turn. The builder answers with a silent wave.

departure_1.narration: You explain which lane is safe and where the wyrm now rests. The builder repeats the report before lifting the signal cloth.

departure_2.narration: You copy the safe marks onto a fresh page. The original plan stays with the people who are building the room.

ending.narration: The readers have space to work, the wyrm has space to rest, and the old ice has been left quiet. A builder hangs the chisel hats beside the doorway. The glacier is a changed place when you leave it, because of something your party chose and did.

variants.text: The original doorway still belongs to the wyrm. The readers work down the tunnel, and their new room is a task for another day.
From the sheltered hollow comes a soft answering rumble. The builders will keep that approach open if your party needs help here again.
The new chamber must wait. Today the readers share their old room with the extra table, and the builders give up their free morning to finish the move.
